req.title: Login required for delete
req.statement: The system shall redirect anonymous users to /auth/login when they POST /<id>/delete.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-014 requires that anonymous (unauthenticated) users who POST to /<id>/delete are redirected to /auth/login. Three test cases are designed: (1) positive — anonymous POST to a valid post id redirects to /auth/login with status 302 and exact Location header; (2) negative — an authenticated user POSTing to their own post's delete endpoint is NOT redirected to login (gets 302 to index instead), confirming the guard only fires for anonymous users; (3) boundary — anonymous POST to a non-existent post id (id=0, boundary below valid range) still hits the login_required decorator before any DB lookup, so the redirect to /auth/login must still occur with status 302. Each test uses exact status code and Location header assertions to kill comparison-operator and constant mutations.

tests.name: test_anonymous_post_delete_redirects_to_login
preconditions: Application is initialised with test database containing pre-loaded rows
No user is logged in (anonymous session)
Post id=1 exists in the database (author_id=5, James)
actions: Create Flask test app with TESTING=True and a temp database
Initialise the database with init_db()
POST to /1/delete without any session cookie
expected: HTTP response status code is exactly 302
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_anonymous_post_delete_redirects_to_login():
    r = client.post('/1/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

tests.name: test_authenticated_post_delete_does_not_redirect_to_login
preconditions: Application is initialised with test database containing pre-loaded rows
User James (id=5, password='river') is logged in
Post id=1 exists and is authored by James (author_id=5)
actions: Create Flask test app with TESTING=True and a temp database
Initialise the database with init_db()
POST to /auth/login with username=James, password=river
POST to /1/delete in the same session
expected: HTTP response status code is exactly 302
trace: R-FLASKR-014: authenticated user must NOT be redirected to /auth/login on delete
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_authenticated_post_delete_does_not_redirect_to_login():
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'James', 'password': 'river'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/1/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] != '/auth/login'
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_anonymous_post_delete_redirect_is_not_200_or_404():
    r = client.post('/2/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.status_code != 200
    assert r.status_code != 403
    assert r.status_code != 404
    assert r.status_code != 500
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
    assert r.headers['Location'] != '/'

tests.name: test_anonymous_post_delete_session_state_transition
preconditions: Application is initialised with test database containing pre-loaded rows
Client starts with no session (anonymous state)
actions: Create Flask test app with TESTING=True and a temp database
Initialise the database with init_db()
In anonymous state: POST to /7/delete
Verify redirect to /auth/login
Log in as Anjali
Verify now authenticated (login returns 302 to /)
POST to /7/delete again as authenticated user
Verify redirect is to / not /auth/login
trace: R-FLASKR-014: state transition from anonymous to authenticated changes delete redirect target
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_anonymous_post_delete_session_state_transition():
    r_anon = client.post('/7/delete')
    assert r_anon.status_code == 302
    assert r_anon.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    assert login_r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    r_auth = client.post('/7/delete')
    assert r_auth.status_code == 302
    assert r_auth.headers['Location'] == '/'
    assert r_auth.headers['Location'] != '/auth/login'
